Order No.05 /Dated: 18 August, 2023
1 .  Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.P.P. for the State.

2. This second bail application has been filed on behalf of the abovenamed applicant with prayer to release on bail in connection with Panki P.S. Case No.139 of 2020 registered under Sections 419,
420, 406 and 311 of the Indian Penal Code pending in the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Daltonganj, Palamau.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that earlier the prayer for bail of the applicant has been rejected by this Court vide order dated 17th October, 2022 passed in B.A. No.7989 of 2022.

By way of present bail application, the applicant has renewed his prayer for bail primarily for the reasons that after rejection of first bail application, the informant was also made accused on the ground that the huge amount of the informant and other victims was duped by applicant having promoted the investors to invest in the company.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has further submitted that by considering the paragraph Nos.434, 443, 450 and 451 of the supplementary case diary, the applicant may be given privilege of bail.
4. Learned APP opposed the contentions made by the learned counsel for the applicant.

5. The first bail application of the applicant was rejected on merit.

6. From perusal of the rejection of the first bail application, it is evident that the first bail application of the applicant was rejected on the ground that the applicant was the promoter of the said company for Jharkhand area and the huge amount of informant and other victims, which was handed over to the Mushtaque Ansari (the present applicant) which was duped by the him by promoting the investors to invest their hard-earned money in the company.
During investigation, this informant was also made accused.

7. In paragraph No.434 of the supplementary case diary, it came that the money of 143 customers including the informant, total of 144 persons amounting Rs.1,34,00,000/- was deposited by the informant in Been Distribution Company, who also lodged the FIR against this applicant.
8. In paragraph No.443 of the supplementary case diary, it came that the informant Nasim Sai was also the agent of the said company.

The customers, namely, Deepak Kumar, Pradeep Kumar Gupta,
Rukmini Gupta, Binod Kumar, Md. Aslam, Md. Arma Alam and Surendra Kumar all have stated that the amount was deposited through Nasim Sai in the company and the panic was created by the informant Nasim Sai not to name him and money was to be taken from Mushtaque Ansari and he has told that there was no complicity of Mushtaque Ansari.

9. In paragraph No.450 of the supplementary case diary, it is stated that Nasim Sai and Mushtaque Ansari both were the agent of the company and the amount of Rs.1,34,00,000/- was deposited in the company.
When the money was demanded by the customers from Nasim Sai and Mushtaque Ansari, who made the pretext and also assured that the money will be doubled.
In paragraph No.451 of the supplementary case diary, the same kind of statement is stated.

10. In view of these paragraph Nos.434, 443, 450 and 451 of the supplementary case diary, it cannot be accepted that the present applicant was exonerated from the charge levelled against him rather the informant, who was also implicated as an accused along with this present applicant, the role of the applicant is shown along with the informant in duping the hard earned money of the customers after having assured them to make it double, if they will become investors of the company.
11. In view of the above, no new ground for consideration of the second bail application is made out.
Accordingly, the same is hereby rejected.

(Subhash Chand, J.) Madhav/-
